summary: Dependency-confusion beacon exfiltrates installer host metadata to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint
details: Package in the @ecg-internal scope ships a postinstall script (`node beacon.cjs`) that POSTs a JSON payload containing the package name, os.hostname(), __dirname install path, process.cwd(), and process.version to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc at `npm install` time. The package `main` (index.js) additionally invokes `require('./beacon.cjs').fire()` unconditionally at module load, so any require/import of the package re-fires the beacon. The module exports a Proxy of no-op functions so that consumer builds continue to succeed after the beacon runs. The scope name, stub no-op surface, and host/path identifiers in the payload are consistent with a dependency-confusion attack targeting an internal `@ecg-internal` namespace, leaking internal hostnames and build layout to an external attacker-controlled IP.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
